question: The operators: which companies and networks run it, and how far along is each?
answer: This page reads every operator the library tracks and how far along each one is, in one status vocabulary: 16 banks and asset managers across seven capabilities with where the proof stops, 32 card and processor products, 12 market systems, the money-machine seats; the bank transition, corporate stack and stack expansion comparisons; the Crypto Hub's 23 families with all 302 nodes and 372 connections; the field guide, the build-out ledger and the 112 vetted October 19 updates; and the 220 named actors and every placement. Announced is not live, and a partnership is not control.

rows.title: J.P. Morgan
fields: Dimension label: Client access · Status: limited · Plain: Institutional clients and named banks use J.P. Morgan's Kinexys blockchain products for payments, financing and tokenization in several regions. · Library code: M5 · Status note: Live, limited (Katie's rule, 2026-10-19): Kinexys products are offered to J.P. Morgan's institutional clients; J.P. Morgan's Oct 19, 2026 release says JPM Coin is 'available to J.P. Morgan's institutional clients'. · Library text: Institutional clients and named banks use Kinexys payment, financing and tokenization products across multiple regions. · Boundary: Eligibility, booking entity and geography vary by product.

Dimension label: Digital money (deposit tokens, stablecoins) · Status: limited · Plain: J.P. Morgan issues deposit tokens (JPM Coin / JPMD) and Blockchain Deposit Accounts, which are claims on J.P. Morgan bank deposits, not stablecoins or central-bank money. · Library code: M5 · Status note: Live, limited (Katie's rule, 2026-10-19): JPM Coin (JPMD) and Blockchain Deposit Accounts are held only by J.P. Morgan's institutional clients. · Library text: Blockchain Deposit Accounts and JPM Coin represent J.P. Morgan deposit claims. · Boundary: They are not common interbank money or central-bank money.

Dimension label: Tokenized assets and records · Status: live · Plain: Kinexys runs tokenization and fund-flow services and supports J.P. Morgan Asset Management's tokenized money-market funds on public Ethereum. · Since: 2026-05-14 · Library code: M5 · Library text: Kinexys operates tokenization, fund-flow and digital-debt services and now supports J.P. Morgan Asset Management tokenized MMFs on public Ethereum. · Boundary: The fund, transfer agent and product terms remain authoritative; Kinexys supplies the translation and tokenization layer.

Dimension label: Custody and keys · Status: limited · Plain: Kinexys keeps the platform records for specific digital-asset workflows; this is not a general crypto-custody service. · Library code: M4 · Library text: Kinexys controls platform records and entitlements for identified digital-asset workflows. · Boundary: This is not proof of a general crypto-custody service for all clients and assets.

Dimension label: Payment and settlement · Status: limited · Plain: Bank-money payments and financing settle repeatedly on Kinexys; KB Kookmin Bank added a named import-export route, and Project Acacia was a controlled repo trial in Australia. · Library code: M5 · Status note: Live, limited (Katie's rule, 2026-10-19): Bank-money payments on Kinexys run between J.P. Morgan's own clients. · Library text: Recurring bank-money flows and financing operate on Kinexys; KB Kookmin added a named bank/corporate import-export route and Acacia added a controlled multi-platform repo test. · Boundary: The Kookmin service remains route- and currency-bounded; Acacia was a controlled trial and external cash/finality rules remain separate.

Dimension label: Collateral and financing · Status: limited · Plain: Kinexys Digital Financing and the Tokenized Collateral Network handle repeat secured-financing and collateral work, which does not make those assets eligible at every clearinghouse. · Library code: M5 · Status note: Live, limited (Katie's rule, 2026-10-19): Kinexys Digital Financing and the Tokenized Collateral Network are J.P. Morgan's own client network. · Library text: Digital Financing and the Tokenized Collateral Network support recurring secured-financing and collateral workflows. · Boundary: Product acceptance does not establish universal CCP eligibility.

Dimension label: Scale (library column 'Scale & recovery'; measures scale only) · Status: limited · Plain: J.P. Morgan reports large repeat volume on Kinexys (over $4 trillion since inception and over $7 billion a day on average, per its June 29, 2026 release) but no public stress, correction or recovery case. · Library code: M5 · Status note: Live, limited (Katie's rule, 2026-10-19): Scale of a client-only network (follows the service's own step). · Library text: J.P. Morgan reports material recurring aggregate volume across Kinexys and named bank/client expansion. · Boundary: No public product-level stress, correction, default or legacy-retirement record was located.
Product name: JPM Coin (JPMD) deposit token; Kinexys Blockchain Deposit Accounts
Chain: Kinexys private ledger (Blockchain Deposit Accounts); JPMD on public Ethereum and Base (J.P. Morgan product page, checked 2026-10-19); Canton integration described as underway

Plain: J.P. Morgan's deposit tokens are live for institutional clients: Blockchain Deposit Accounts run on J.P. Morgan's private ledger in eight currencies, and the JPMD dollar token runs on Ethereum and Base.
Status note: Status is 'limited' because the service is open only to the bank's own eligible institutional clients (Katie's definition, 2026-10-19).
J.P. Morgan June 29, 2026 Kinexys release and JPM Coin product page checked 2026-10-19 (volumes, currencies, JPMD chains).
Per-capability start dates are not recorded in the library; 'since' is filled only where one dated launch source exists.
Start dates for Blockchain Deposit Accounts and JPMD are not recorded in the library.
Has JPMD's Canton integration gone live?
Thesis: Use regulated bank money and institution-grade public/private-chain infrastructure as the trust anchor for always-on payments, financing and assets.
Frontier: Joining proprietary bank money, financing and public-chain assets without fragmenting liquidity.
Watch: Route-level volumes and a public correction, default or recovery case.

rows.title: DTC Tokenization Service
fields: The Depository Trust Company (DTC), a DTCC subsidiary; software from DTCC Digital (US)

Lets DTC participants (the brokers and banks that hold securities at DTC) turn selected securities into tokens on approved blockchains and back again. DTC's own system (LedgerScan) stays the official record of who holds the tokens, and Cede & Co. stays the registered holder on the issuer's books. Eligible: Russell 1000 stocks, ETFs tracking major indexes, and U.S. Treasury bills, notes and bonds. At first the tokens carry no collateral or settlement value inside DTC.

Settled label: LIMITED. DTCC itself called the July 2026 run 'initial, limited production trades' (May 4 release) and the Jul 15 run used DTC's real production environment with real securities for several hours. It is not 'live': DTCC's own page still said 'expected October 2026 launch' when checked on 2026-10-19, and no DTCC announcement of the general launch was found. A KuCoin news flash (Oct 17) says the service launched for 25 securities, citing 'DTCC documentation'; this is unconfirmed.

SEC staff no-action letter (Division of Trading and Markets), Dec 11, 2025: staff will not recommend enforcement if DTC launches a 'Preliminary Base Version'; the relief ends three years after launch. It is a staff position, not a Commission rule, and can be changed or withdrawn.
Date: 2025-12-11 · Status: announced · What: SEC staff no-action letter allows DTC to launch the tokenization service's first version for three years; DTC expected launch in the second half of 2026.
Date: 2025-12-17 · Status: announced · What: DTCC and Digital Asset announce a plan to tokenize DTC-held U.S. Treasuries on Canton.
Date: 2026-05-04 · Status: announced · What: DTCC plans 'initial, limited production trades' in July 2026 and a service launch in October 2026; more than 50 firms in its industry working group.
Date: 2026-05-27 · Status: announced · What: DTCC and the Stellar Development Foundation expect DTC-tokenized assets on Stellar in the first half of 2027.

Date: 2026-07-15 · Status: limited · What: First production trades with DTC-tokenized assets over several hours: collateral pledges, securities lending, Treasury repo and stock trades where security and cash swap at once, and clearinghouse margin. DTCC's release says more than 30 firms; its later page says about 40. Networks: DTCC's private Besu network and the public Canton network.

rows.title: Swift blockchain-based shared ledger
fields: S.W.I.F.T. SC (Swift, a bank-owned Belgian cooperative company)

A shared ledger run by Swift on which participating banks record and move tokenized deposits that they themselves issue, around the clock including weekends. Swift coordinates the payment commitments; final settlement still happens afterwards through existing payment systems, and each bank stays responsible for its own deposits.

rows.title: No public receipt

fields: Institution-authored analysis, strategy or forecast without a corresponding operating commitment.

rows.title: Announced build
fields: Roadmap, intended launch, consortium exploration or conditional approval; not yet an operating receipt.

rows.title: Pilot / test
fields: Controlled experiment, sandbox, proof of concept or trial.

fields: Completed transaction or live product with a narrow client, product, jurisdiction or event perimeter.

fields: Recurring scale plus public stress, correction, recovery, default or legacy-retirement evidence.

fields: Can eligible clients enter, trade, hold or use digital products through the institution?

fields: Does the group issue or operate a deposit token, tokenized deposit, stablecoin or other on-chain cash claim?

fields: Does it operate regulated custody, wallet, key or digital-asset servicing capability?

fields: Connects incumbent custody, transfer agency, fund accounting and cash books to token and wallet systems.

rows.title: Capital-markets manufacturer
fields: Builds issuance, trading, financing or lifecycle infrastructure for digital securities and collateral.

rows.title: Client gateway
fields: Provides research, access or distribution while proprietary digital money and settlement infrastructure remains limited or developing.

fields: Places a regulated fund share, security or e-money claim directly on public networks through an identified issuer and record structure.

rows.title: Ondo U.S. / Oasis Pro stack

The ATS and transfer-agent registrations do not make Ondo or an affiliate a TSV, and the U.S. custodial entitlement model is not the same product as Ondo's global synthetic/custodial offerings or the proposed Ondo Network.

Oasis Pro Markets joined DTCC Fund/SERV on September 16, and Ondo Stocks added live case-by-case institutional in-kind conversion through Alpaca on Ethereum and BNB Chain on September 21.
Fund/SERV membership and an approved-institution conversion route do not prove general retail access, recurring volume, shareholder title onchain or Ondo Network production.

Fit: capability · Note: Broker-dealer, transfer-agent and custodian controls enforce participant and transfer restrictions.
Fit: capability · Note: Oasis Pro TA issues tokenized entitlements while underlying shares stay in the incumbent custody chain and Broadridge supports holder communications and proxy.

Commencement notice, participants, eligible securities, DTC participation, corporate-action processing, operational volumes and the later permanent-registration state.
The current reviewed record remains temporary clearing-agency registration and amended operating materials; no later commencement or production-volume receipt was located through September 27.

tZERO announced a September 14 financing round to advance its tokenized-market infrastructure-as-a-service offering and support a possible strategic transaction.
Funding and strategic intent do not establish a new operating route, eligible-security cohort, transaction volume or completed corporate transaction.
Fit: capability · Note: A registered ATS is a live venue comparator but not the new exempt venue category.
Fit: capability · Note: Broker-dealer onboarding and eligibility sit in the access layer.

rows.title: Broadridge governance services
fields: Broadridge can carry proxy voting, issuer communications and regulatory disclosures into tokenized-security arrangements.
Governance servicing is not the transfer agent's authoritative ownership record, the custodian's position, venue operation or settlement finality.
Issuer mandates, account and token-holder reconciliation, vote entitlement proofs, distribution completion and correction records.
Broadridge launched DLX on September 9 as a multi-chain orchestration layer connecting tokenization, trading, settlement, books and records, custody, wallets and established market systems.
Platform launch and stated DTCC/Canton connectivity do not prove every module, client workflow or asset class is in production.
Fit: capability · Note: ProxyVote and communications fill a rights-servicing sublayer that a token contract alone does not provide.
Fit: support · Note: The service must reconcile token-holder data to the incumbent shareholder communications chain.

rows.title: Fireblocks + Tokeny / ERC-3643
fields: Wallet policy, issuance and transfer-control tooling
Permissioned token controls on public chains
Fireblocks key and policy tooling plus Tokeny's ERC-3643 contracts can combine secure signing, mint/burn functions, identity checks, transfer restrictions, freeze, pause and recovery controls.
Technical control does not itself supply broker-dealer, transfer-agent, venue, custodian or title authority, and ERC-3643 documentation's ownership language remains product- and law-dependent.
Exact contract deployment, authorized claim issuers, compliance modules, key holders, upgrade and recovery powers, regulated agents and register reconciliation.
Fireblocks reported that its wallet infrastructure supported Citadel Securities in DTCC's July limited-production tokenization event and current Canton connectivity.
A participant's limited-production wallet use does not prove general DTCC service launch, Tokeny use, authoritative title or scaled volume.
Fit: capability · Note: The combined stack directly addresses signing policy and token-level transfer eligibility.
Fit: support · Note: It can execute issuance and recovery instructions but does not determine which external register legally controls.
Fit: capability · Note: Lifecycle APIs connect issuer, wallet and distribution systems while exact failure authority must be disclosed.

rows.title: Anchorage + BitGo custody comparison
fields: Anchorage and BitGo show why legal custody, key control, segregation, wallet policy and movement authorization must be mapped separately from the venue and chain.
A custodian's charter or trust status does not make it the issuer, transfer agent, clearing agency, TSV operator or cash-settlement bank for a particular stock pool.
Named product mandate, exact legal entity, asset eligibility, segregation, subcustody, insolvency treatment, settlement instruction and incident receipts.
The reviewed custody layer remains live and product-specific; no single new September receipt changed the requirement to identify the exact custodian entity, mandate, asset and movement authority.
General custody capability is not evidence that Anchorage or BitGo serves a particular tokenized-security route.
Fit: capability · Note: Custody platforms manage keys, approvals and movement controls.
Fit: capability · Note: Legal custody and reconciliation are post-trade functions; product-specific securities settlement remains separate.
Fit: support · Note: Custody APIs can attach wallets and settlement instructions to external venues.

rows.title: AMM + solver family
fields: UniswapX, CoW Protocol and 1inch execution patterns
Pools, intents, solvers, routers and fillers
AMMs and intent-based systems expose different execution designs: pool curves, signed orders, auctions, solver competition, offchain liquidity and onchain settlement checks.

Execution software does not supply the TSV operator, participant eligibility, securities rights, Covered Firm status, surveillance, clearing or cash finality. A filler is not automatically the order's qualifying liquidity provider.
Exact public code, contract addresses, permissioning wrapper, pool assets, parameter and pause authority, filler identity, inventory source and execution receipts.
Uniswap introduced permissioned v4 pools for regulated assets, while CoW's Bring Your Own Solver work reached a BNB staging settlement environment by September 25.
A generalized hook standard and staging solver receipt do not establish a production regulated market, lawful venue or dependable liquidity for a named security.
Fit: capability · Note: The family broadens the application layer beyond one AMM curve.
Fit: candidate · Note: Solvers and fillers may source liquidity or use inventory, but the exact legal actor and statutory conditions must be proven separately.
Fit: support · Note: Cross-chain designs add settlement-oracle and bridge dependencies.

sources.label: CoW Bring Your Own Solver staging receipt

rows.title: Kinexys Digital Payments / JPM Coin
fields: Deposit claim on JPMorgan Chase Bank
Kinexys shows a tokenized commercial-bank deposit model in which the bank remains the obligor and operates the private payments ledger.
A bank deposit token is not a stablecoin, central-bank money, public-DLT venue or proof of completed payment for a named TSV trade.
Named TSV cash-leg agreement, eligible users, deposit terms, ledger and bank-book postings, external payout and reconciliation receipts.
KB Kookmin Bank became the first Korean bank named as using the Kinexys Blockchain Deposit Account network for import and export payments on September 2.
A named bank use does not make JPM Coin a universal settlement asset or establish volume, external-bank finality or use in every trade flow.
Fit: candidate · Note: A bank deposit claim is a possible cash asset around a venue only if the order permits the category and the exact arrangement selects it.
Fit: capability · Note: The bank ledger can complete cash delivery among admitted clients, subject to its own terms.

rows.title: Partior
fields: Participating-bank deposit liabilities on a shared network
Partior demonstrates synchronized movement of commercial-bank-money claims across participating banks and currencies.
The network does not become the obligor for every represented deposit, a U.S. TSV, a public permissionless ledger or central-bank money.
Named banks, currency, account claims, transaction completion, customer credit, default rules and any direct TSV connection.
Partior and LSEG Digital Settlement House announced a September 17 collaboration intended to supply always-on settlement-bank liquidity across participating banks.
Strategic collaboration and intended liquidity movement are not a production integration, named transaction or removal of bank-liability boundaries.
Fit: capability · Note: The network coordinates bank-money settlement while each bank retains its liability.
Fit: capability · Note: Multi-bank orchestration is its core relevance to an external trading venue.

sources.label: Partior and LSEG DiSH settlement-liquidity collaboration

rows.title: Fnality / Sterling Fnality Payment System
fields: DLT settlement asset backed through a Bank of England omnibus account
Fnality supplies a distinct wholesale-settlement model linked to central-bank funds and operated under recognized-payment-system supervision.
It is not a U.S. cash rail, unrestricted central-bank money for the public, a stablecoin or evidence of settlement for a named U.S. TSV trade.
Operating limits, participant roster, transaction scale, legal claim structure, default rules and any cross-border securities link.
Sterling Fnality remains a live supervised wholesale settlement comparator under the operating limits described by the Bank of England; no material September expansion receipt was located.
Live supervised operation does not establish unrestricted scale, cross-currency reach or use in a named tokenized-security route.
Fit: capability · Note: The system is a concrete wholesale cash-settlement comparison, not a U.S. venue component by default.
Fit: support · Note: External securities systems would require explicit integration and failure rules.

rows.title: CAT and regulatory event reporting
fields: Lifecycle event reporting to a regulatory repository
CAT illustrates the separate reporting layer needed to reconstruct order and trade events across participants rather than relying on public-chain visibility alone.
Regulatory reporting is not market surveillance by itself, public transaction publication, venue operation or proof of legal settlement.
Order-specific reportable events, clocks, identifiers, linkage, correction, validation and regulator acceptance receipts.
CAT's official FAQ was updated September 23 and continues to require order, quote, routing, execution and correction events for NMS and OTC equity securities irrespective of an onchain record.
CAT coverage does not make blockchain events self-reporting or prove that a tokenization route has produced accepted CAT records.
Fit: capability · Note: CAT-like reporting fills the regulator-facing event ledger sublayer.
Fit: support · Note: The venue must connect its onchain and offchain event model to accepted regulatory reports.

rows.title: Nasdaq SMARTS surveillance
fields: Cross-market manipulation monitoring and alert workflow
SMARTS illustrates why market-abuse detection, alerting and investigation are distinct from an oracle price or an immutable transaction log.
Surveillance software does not itself halt a market, adjudicate misconduct, create regulatory reports, operate the venue or guarantee complete data coverage.
Named deployment, data feeds, alert scenarios, human escalation, halt authority, retention, false-positive review and incident receipts.
Nasdaq and Payward expanded their relationship on September 10 with a market-surveillance agreement covering crypto, equities and tokenized equities alongside NET framework work.
An agreement to adopt surveillance technology is not an operating alert, completed deployment, regulatory-reporting receipt or halt authority.
Fit: capability · Note: Surveillance analytics fill a separate sublayer from price formation and reporting.
Fit: support · Note: The system depends on complete venue, reference-market and participant data feeds.

fields: xStocks provide a live, multichain, DeFi-composable comparison for one-for-one backed exposure and cash-value redemption outside the U.S. offering perimeter.

Backed states the products are not registered or offered to U.S. persons. They are not the underlying issuer's common stock and do not demonstrate U.S. TSV eligibility, shareholder title or voting rights.
Exact prospectus, issuer, custodian, reserve proof, rights, corporate actions, redemption, venue and jurisdiction restrictions.
Kraken's September 18 FAQ records 131 xStocks across Solana, Ethereum, TON and Ink for eligible non-U.S. users, with price exposure rather than shareholder title or voting rights.
Distributor availability and one-for-one backing do not confer underlying-company shareholder rights or U.S. availability.
Fit: outside · Note: Useful rights-model comparison, but not a U.S. tokenized NMS stock seat occupant.
Fit: capability · Note: The tokens demonstrate composability with crypto applications outside the U.S. order's product perimeter.

rows.title: Dinari dShares
fields: Custodially backed token with claimed economic and corporate-action rights

Dinari offers a different comparison model: underlying securities in a custodial brokerage account, claimed economic rights, mirrored splits, stablecoin dividends and token-level eligibility controls.

The public description is company-authored and the product is offered outside the U.S.; it does not establish issuer-register title, U.S. NMS trading, TSV qualification or the same legal rights as the Ondo U.S. model.
Exact issuer and offering documents, custodian, beneficial-interest record, voting, dividends, redemption, jurisdiction and regulatory status.
Dinari brought dShares to Arc mainnet on September 16 after a September 15 live U.S. Bitcoin.com distribution launch for eligible users.
Network and distributor availability do not establish issuer-register title, universal eligibility, transaction scale or identical rights across jurisdictions.
Fit: capability · Note: The model describes token-level KYC, geography and eligibility controls.

rows.title: Ripple / XRPL
fields: Follow Ripple from the operating company through acquired product lines, exact regulated entities, RLUSD and XRP, XRPL transport, market access and the SEC proposal overlap.
Ripple, its subsidiaries and products, XRPL, XRP and RLUSD are separate legal and technical objects; an edge records a reviewed relationship, not a merger of roles.
Steering: Ripple is the company parent; XRPL is a public network rather than a Ripple-owned subsidiary.

Treasury and lending: Evernorth and Pathfinder are separate legal entities from Ripple; pre-close XRP remains under exact custody and escrow restrictions, while Evernorth's Single Asset Vault and XLS-66 participation remains proposed.
Execution: XRPL provides ledger, DEX and pathfinding functions; Wormhole and the XRPL EVM sidechain extend transport and application reach.

Legal endpoint: Customer, issuer, custodian, transfer-agent and market-utility records remain decisive for title, redemption and settlement.

rows.title: SEC proposal 34-106246

rows.title: Registered recordkeeping transfer agent

rows.title: Authoritative master securityholder file

fields: Client teams implement the protocol software used by nodes and validators.

rows.title: Ethereum issuers and application operators
fields: Issuers, custodians and application operators control contracts, redemptions and off-chain legal obligations for their own assets.
Their authority is not Ethereum protocol ownership and must be evaluated product by product.

sections.title: Field guide: what each technology is and what it does not control
sections.sub: A differentiator is a useful architectural or operating distinction, not proof of adoption, market power, legal authority, production scale or token value capture.
sections.home: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Tokenization Entity and Control Map 2026-09-01/technology_field_guide.json
sections.part: 4 · Field guide, build-out ledger and the October 19 updates

rows.title: Company & operating stack
fields: A legal company group, regulated subsidiaries and products. It may use networks, but it is not the network.

rows.title: Public base network
fields: Shared transaction infrastructure operated under protocol rules. Its native token is one object on the network, not the network itself.

rows.title: Institutional network
fields: A governed coordination environment designed around institutional participants, privacy or controlled workflows.

rows.title: Connector & middleware
fields: Software that carries data, messages or instructions between systems without becoming the issuer or authoritative record.

rows.title: Market infrastructure
fields: An incumbent regulated or bank-coordination system whose records and rules can create legal or operational effect.

rows.title: Money-claim family
fields: A comparison of liabilities and settlement forms rather than one company or network.

rows.title: Ripple is not XRPL—and neither is XRP or RLUSD
fields: Ripple is the operating company and product stack. XRPL is a public network. XRP is its native asset. RLUSD is a separately issued stablecoin claim. Their success, control and evidence ledgers must stay separate.

rows.title: Securitize is not Ethereum
fields: Securitize supplies regulated issuer, transfer-agent, brokerage/ATS, advisory and administration roles through named entities. Ethereum supplies public execution and consensus. A token can run on Ethereum while its legal ownership record and investor rights remain with Securitize, the issuer and governing documents.

rows.title: Solana is the network; SOL is the native asset
fields: Solana names the protocol, runtime and validator network. SOL pays fees and supports staking. Issued assets and applications on Solana retain their own operators, controls and legal records.

rows.title: Ripple / XRPL
fields: A company-centered institutional digital-asset stack attached to, but legally separate from, the public XRP Ledger.

Ripple is assembling payments, custody, prime brokerage, treasury, wallet and stablecoin capabilities around institutional movement of value, while XRP Asia now adds a separable regional builder and systems-integrator distribution layer. That makes the stack relevant far beyond the retail idea of a payments coin.

The breadth of the operating stack: company products and acquired regulated entities can touch customer access, custody, liquidity, treasury and cash-like claims while XRPL supplies a separate public execution and pathfinding layer.
Breadth does not make Ripple the owner of XRPL, the issuer of every XRPL asset, the legal recordkeeper for every tokenized security or proof that XRP is required in every Ripple route.

A builder may enter upstream through XRP Asia, the XRP Ledger Foundation, XRPL Commons or another separate ecosystem-support body; those organizations do not inherit Ripple licences or product authority.
A customer or institution enters through a Ripple product or exact regulated affiliate.
The route may use custody, prime-brokerage, treasury or payment services depending on the job.
XRPL can provide ledger, exchange and pathfinding functions; XRP or RLUSD may play different asset roles.
Banks, issuers, custodians and legal recordkeepers still complete cash, title, redemption and remedy.
Product design and commercial routing choices
Certain issued-asset or custody functions through named entities
An issuer's legal register or bank settlement merely because the route touches Ripple technology
Multiple current operating products and completed acquisitions coexist with conditional, proposed and advocacy-stage elements.

XRP Asia program dates, funding, recipients, systems-integrator contracts and country-lawful mainnet deployments
Operating evidence for conditionally approved or proposed entities and functions

A Ripple policy submission ≠ SEC adoption

rows.title: Securitize
fields: A public tokenization company whose named subsidiaries form a regulated securities-control plane across transfer agency, brokerage/ATS, investment advice, fund administration and an EU DLT trading-and-settlement venue.

It is one of the clearest places to see where a token becomes part of a real security: issuer authority, investor identity, the official register, transfer restrictions, corporate actions, trading access, redemption and correction.

It joins technology with a multi-entity regulated operating stack. Depending on the product, the transfer agent can maintain an off-chain control book across several token representations, a composite blockchain-plus-identity official register, or a token layer linked to an incumbent registrar.
Regulatory registrations belong to exact subsidiaries and activities. They do not make Securitize a blockchain, a universal CSD or the sponsor of every fund it services.
A fund or issuer creates the legal instrument and appoints the exact entities.
The transfer agent binds identity and eligibility to an account or whitelisted wallet and maintains the product-specific official record.
Securitize Markets can place or trade eligible securities; the adviser and administrator perform different appointed jobs.
A supported network carries token state or instructions while outside issuers, custodians and cash providers complete the legal and money legs.
The transfer agent can apply corporate actions and product-specific freeze, burn, reissue or correction procedures.
Its transfer-agent records, identity links, restrictions and correction workflows where appointed
Ethereum, Solana, Tempo or another public network
A fund sponsor's investment mandate or issuer's corporate authority
Bank cash, reserve custody or asset custody outside the appointed arrangement
Every public company's primary register merely because Securitize supplies a token layer
Current U.S. regulated entities, live tokenized products, a 2026 public listing and CNMV-approved EU TSS coexist with partnership and production-volume clocks that remain product-specific.
Which record is legally authoritative for each product
Direct evidence for reported broker-dealer custody and atomic-settlement operations

rows.title: Ethereum
fields: A public smart-contract network with independent clients and validators, an execution environment and the native asset ETH.
It is the most reusable execution layer in this map: issuers, funds, stablecoins, middleware and layer-2 systems can all attach while retaining separate legal authority.

rows.title: Bitcoin

rows.title: Ripple
fields: Ripple's stack combines company-reported live institutional uses with a newly live XRP Asia regional builder layer; the organization expands XRPL distribution capacity without creating a payment route or XRP demand receipt.

CSD BR remains the strongest operating receipt: real BTG Pactual fund-share records, Ripple Custody and XRPL MPTs in a live-environment first phase while CSD BR retains the official registration, deposit and settlement record. XRP Asia is a separate organizational receipt upstream of products and transactions.

sources.label: Supporting Innovation on the XRP Ledger: What's Changing in 2026
CSD BR and Ripple XRPL record-mirroring partnership
Ripple written input to SEC Crypto Task Force

rows.title: Securitize
fields: Securitize remains the clearest regulated issuance, transfer-agent, broker-dealer and fund-services stack in the cohort.
Regulatory filings, BUIDL agreements and 2026 results identify the operating entities, contracts and material tokenized-fund activity.

sources.label: Securitize Q2 2026 results and operating update
BUIDL platform, transfer-agent and registrar agreement
BUIDL Solana launch and seven-network availability

rows.title: Ethereum
fields: Ethereum remains the broadest programmable settlement substrate in the set; its current transition is protocol scaling and user-experience hardening, not a new institutional controller.
The current network is live while Glamsterdam approaches mainnet and Hegotá remains in scoping.

sources.label: BUIDL Solana launch and seven-network availability
Circle Mint supported chains and currencies

rows.title: Hedera
fields: Hedera is pairing council-governed public infrastructure with enterprise token and messaging use, while new cross-ledger work is still standards-stage.
Named Archax and Lloyds collateral uses sit above live consensus/token services; CLPR is a donated lab project, not production settlement.

sources.label: Cross-Ledger Protocol donated to LF Decentralized Trust
Aberdeen, Lloyds and Archax complete tokenized-collateral FX pilot

rows.title: Stellar
fields: Stellar is expanding issuer-controlled payment assets and ramps while carefully staged protocol-upgrade work continues.
USDT0 is live and U.S. Bank completed a bounded inter-entity stablecoin pilot; official network documentation still listed Protocol 27 at cutoff.

sources.label: U.S. Bank stablecoin pilot on Stellar

rows.title: Canton Global Synchronizer
fields: Canton is moving from privacy-preserving institutional connectivity into named collateral, wallet and application integrations, but network-wide aggregates remain operator-reported.
DTCC's limited production trades provide the strongest external receipt for a Canton-connected institutional workflow.

rows.title: Solana
fields: Solana is accumulating consumer and institutional payment access points while core performance work continues.
Named Western Union and MoneyGram products provide operating access, though ecosystem metrics remain foundation-reported.

rows.title: Avalanche
fields: Avalanche continues to specialize in configurable L1 environments; Helicon is the current protocol upgrade, not itself an adoption event.
Evergreen and named L1s remain available while Helicon changes staking, execution and gas mechanics.

sources.label: AVAX token and Primary Network fees

rows.title: Chainlink decentralized oracle networks
fields: Chainlink is becoming a cross-chain data and messaging layer for named institutions; the Reserve creates a bounded LINK accumulation channel, not a holder revenue right.
CCIP has named institutional collaborations and current network support, including Arc mainnet release support.

rows.title: Bitcoin network
fields: Bitcoin remains a narrowly governed monetary network with incremental voluntary software releases and separate Lightning/payment layers.
Bitcoin Core 30.1 is released; node adoption is voluntary and not equivalent to a protocol mandate.

sources.label: BOLT: Basis of Lightning Technology (the Lightning Network specifications)
Bitcoin white paper (Satoshi Nakamoto, 2008): transactions and the network

rows.title: Depository Trust Company
fields: DTCC moved tokenization from authorization and design into a bounded production event; the general service remains on a separate launch clock.
About 40 firms participated in limited production trades involving QQQ, Treasury repo/buy-sell and collateral workflows.

rows.title: Cash legs & tokenized bank money
fields: OUSD adds a live coalition-distributed stablecoin to the fragmented cash-leg field: Bridge owes the claim, Open Standard coordinates partner economics, distributors control access, and four chains carry token state.
OUSD launched with exact native contracts and about $478.5 million of issuer-reported matched supply and reserves, while Bridge terms preserve a separate eligible-user redemption and remedy layer.

Great British Tokenised Deposits live customer transactions
Swift blockchain ledger ready for use
Open Standard company structure and leadership
Mastercard Digital Asset and Stablecoin Solutions — OUSD

rows.title: Circle
fields: Circle now combines a live public Arc mainnet, USDC issuance, CPN payment orchestration and a chartered trust-bank perimeter, each with different clocks.
Arc public mainnet launched September 16 with named validators and integrations; CPN also has named live routes.

sources.label: Circle Form 8-K — Tazapay Share Purchase Agreement
Circle announces agreement to acquire Tazapay

rows.title: Coinbase
fields: Coinbase is extending from exchange/custody into tokenization, Base distribution and bank-facing stablecoin infrastructure, with entity and jurisdiction boundaries still controlling.
Prime and Base are live; Coinbase Tokenize and the filed AAPL structure provide specific issuance architecture rather than a generic platform claim.

rows.title: Algorand
fields: Algorand's 2026 technology story is native post-quantum accounts plus protocol and staking consolidation, alongside bounded tokenized-asset deployments.
Post-quantum account tooling and v5 software are live; named tokenized products exist but do not establish ecosystem scale.

rows.title: XDC Network
fields: XDC remains a trade-finance-oriented EVM network with native USDC/CCTP support, but current official evidence is thinner than its ecosystem marketing.
Native USDC and CCTP V2 are live on XDC; architecture and masternode documentation define the operating network.

sources.label: Native USDC and CCTP V2 on XDC

rows.title: IOTA network
fields: IOTA has moved its Rebased and Starfish protocol work to mainnet while TWIN and ADAPT remain a mixture of live components, pilots and governance buildout.
Starfish and account abstraction are live; TWIN reports anchored trade transactions and named UK work, but scaled operations remain unproved.

rows.title: Wormhole
fields: Wormhole remains an interoperability layer used by named assets and platforms, while product deprecations underline the need to track exact route versions.
RLUSD and Securitize asset routes provide named live integrations; legacy portal routes are being retired.

rows.title: Quant
fields: Quant had the strongest late-September cluster: a live Fusion mainnet, UK tokenized-deposit customer transactions, a Clearing House supplier selection and a Murex integration.
UK Finance reported three live customer transactions on a Quant-built platform; this remains bounded rather than general production.

sources.label: Great British Tokenised Deposits live customer transactions
The Clearing House selects Quant for On-Chain Money Initiative

rows.title: Swift shared ledger
fields: Banks report live controlled payments over Swift's shared ledger across six disclosed pairings, while bank-issued liabilities, external settlement and failure responsibility remain with the banks and existing systems.
DBS reports a September 5 weekend USD payment from Singapore to Citi New York completed in minutes; five other bank-reported pairings bring the bounded disclosed set to eight named banks.
